headlines: Bloom Energy Stock, AI Power Play, Has Room To Run - Investor's Business Daily, 2026-11-19
Bloom Energy Corp (NYSE:BE) stock fell as a broader sell-off in technology and AI-linked stocks weighed on sentiment - Robinhood, 2026-11-20
gappers.catalyst_detail: There is no negative company-specific event. On Nov 19 a Wall Street skeptic (BMO) upgraded BE to Outperform while cutting its price target to $230 from $260, and IBD reported the stock reversed LOWER on that upgrade the same day. It now gaps down a further 6.84% from $168.11 to $156.60. Robinhood's Nov 20 note attributes the decline to 'a broader sell-off in technology and artificial intelligence-linked stocks'. A Benzinga snippet claimed BE was +6.63% premarket on the Anthropic IPO sparking an AI-power rebound; that directly contradicts Alpaca's 09:09 ET snapshot of -6.84% and was DISCARDED in favour of the approved Alpaca source.
gappers.why: Pure beta. BE is the highest-multiple AI-power/fuel-cell proxy on the watchlist, so it absorbs the most selling when the AI complex de-rates. The more telling mechanism is that a genuine analyst UPGRADE was sold into - when good news cannot hold a bid, supply is in control and the marginal buyer has left.
gappers.impact: Reads as a continuation of a complex-wide de-rating rather than a one-day headline spike, but the volume does not support a capitulation call: Nov 19 traded only ~1.4x its 20d average. Orderly distribution, not a climax flush, which argues the de-rating is not finished. Sector read-through is strong and symmetric - all four other gappers today are the same AI-infra/power/semis trade, and BE is the largest mover of the five.
gappers.horizon_reasoning: Headline-and-beta driven with no durable thesis in the tape - the BMO upgrade already failed to hold, so there is nothing structural to carry past the week.
gappers.opportunity_cost: The account is 100% cash with zero open positions, so this displaces no existing holding. What it would actually spend is one of 3 weekly trade slots (0/3 used, week of Nov 16) on a counter-trend catch in a sector the market is actively de-rating - directly against the rulebook's 'follow sector momentum'. It also cannot clear the 2:1 R:R minimum at a sane stop: the mandated 10% trailing stop on a $156.60 entry sits near $141, so 2:1 demands a ~$188 target (+20%), i.e. a full recovery above the pre-selloff $168 close, which no one-day bounce delivers. Fails the gate on both momentum and R:R.

Unusual Machines (UMAC) PT Raised to $40 at Roth/MKM - StreetInsider

gappers.catalyst_detail: No new company-specific disclosure today. UMAC is continuing to unwind the pop from its recent Oppenheimer initiation (Outperform, $30 PT), a move that was analyst-sponsored rather than earnings-driven and therefore had no fundamental floor. Compounding it, a Nov 18 notice on LD Micro flags potential securities claims being gathered against drone peer Red Cat Holdings, which taints sentiment across the small-cap drone group. UMAC also has a documented history of equity offerings diluting rallies.
gappers.why: A low-float microcap whose rally was built on analyst sponsorship, not cash flow, unwinds fastest when risk appetite drops - there is no valuation anchor to defend. The Red Cat investigation supplies a group-level reason to reduce drone exposure, and the dilution track record means holders expect any strength to be sold into an offering.
gappers.impact: The ~2.0x volume ratio is the strongest of the five, so this move has real participation rather than drift - but in a $9.59 microcap that cuts both ways: thin liquidity exaggerates both the drop and any bounce. Reads as a genuine position-reduction, not a headline blip. Read-through is to the small-cap drone group (Red Cat) rather than to the AI-infra complex, making UMAC the one name here moving for partly its own reasons.
gappers.horizon_reasoning: Unwinding an analyst-initiation pop in a microcap with a dilution history and a peer under securities investigation - no structural catalyst, expect continued fade.
gappers.opportunity_cost: Nothing to displace (zero positions, 100% cash). The binding cost is a weekly trade slot plus the position-sizing math: ATR-based sizing on a $9.59 microcap this volatile would either demand a stop far wider than 10% or a position too small to matter, and the 20%-of-equity cap is irrelevant when the real limit is UMAC's liquidity. At a 10% trailing stop (~$8.63) the 2:1 minimum needs ~$11.51, above the $10.15 prior close - achievable only if the whole drone group reverses, which the Red Cat overhang argues against. Worst risk-adjusted candidate of the five.

headlines: Nebius Group NBIS Jumps As AI Contract Fuels Volatile Trading - StocksToTrade, 2026-08-12 (prior-cycle context)
gappers.catalyst_detail: Nothing fresh fired today - this is the continuation of a post-Q3 de-rating. At Q3, Nebius guided 2026 revenue to the LOW end of its $3.0-3.4B range while simultaneously raising 2026 capex to roughly $27B, citing data-center build delays. That combination - less revenue, more spend, slower delivery - is the core of the move; the stock is now more than 57% off its October high and roughly 43% lower over 30 days. Today's -5.49% is that trend continuing under the Nov 19 market-wide risk-off, not a new disclosure.
gappers.why: A guidance reset that cuts revenue while raising capex forces a direct repricing of the discounted cash flows: the cash-burn window widens and the payback moves further out. In a tightening-credit tape, a capex-heavy, pre-profit neocloud is exactly the profile that loses its multiple first - and the Anthropic IPO absorbing AI capital on Nov 19 gave holders a concrete reason to fund the new issue by selling the incumbent.
gappers.impact: Only ~1.1x average volume means today's leg is passive drift and sympathy selling rather than fresh capitulation - no evidence of a seller-exhaustion bottom. Given the stock is already -57% from its high WITHOUT a climax-volume flush, the base case is further grind lower. Read-through is direct to CRWV (rank 4), the other neocloud here, which is gapping -5.28% on the same thesis - confirming this is a group de-rating.
gappers.horizon_reasoning: The driver is a structural guidance reset (revenue to the low end, capex to ~$27B), not a headline - but it is structurally NEGATIVE, so LONG_TERM describes the durability of the de-rating, not a reason to own it.
gappers.opportunity_cost: No holding to displace. Taking it would spend a weekly slot buying a name whose own guidance says revenue is tracking to the low end while capex rises - the opposite of the rulebook's confluence requirement, and in a sector already showing two consecutive failed down-days (the 'exit a sector after 2 failed trades' spirit). On R:R: a 10% trailing stop from $91.60 sits near $82.44, so 2:1 needs ~$110 - above the $96.92 prior close and requiring a ~20% retrace inside a -57% downtrend. Does not clear the minimum.

headlines: CoreWeave's (CRWV) AI Growth Faces Mounting Debt - Markets Insider
CoreWeave (CRWV) Gets a Hold from Barclays - Markets Insider
No verified news or fundamental catalyst found for the intraday reversal; likely profit-taking after the +21% post-earnings move - Tickeron, 2026-11-08
gappers.catalyst_detail: No new disclosure today. CoreWeave's problem is its capital structure, not its demand: Q3 revenue grew ~168% and backlog stands near $132.5B, yet the market is repricing roughly $35.6B of debt that now carries a ~16% debt yield against a 7.9% cost of debt. Markets Insider's standing headline is 'CoreWeave's AI Growth Faces Mounting Debt', and Barclays carries a Hold. Today's -5.28% is that repricing continuing through the Nov 19 broad selloff.
gappers.why: When a leveraged growth name's debt yield (~16%) runs far above its coupon (7.9%), the credit market is pricing real default risk, and equity is the residual claim - so the equity de-rates even as revenue compounds. The Anthropic IPO pulling AI capital into a new, unlevered issue on Nov 19 sharpened the contrast: investors can own AI exposure without CRWV's balance sheet.
gappers.impact: At ~1.8x average volume this is the second-most-participated move of the five, consistent with genuine institutional de-risking rather than a headline spike. It is unlikely to mean-revert cleanly because the driver is a credit repricing, which resolves over quarters, not days. Direct read-through to NBIS (rank 3), the other neocloud, down -5.49% on the same group thesis.
gappers.horizon_reasoning: A capital-structure repricing at ~$35.6B debt and a 16% debt yield is structural and slow-resolving - but structurally negative, so LONG_TERM marks the durability of the overhang, not a swing-long thesis.
gappers.opportunity_cost: Nothing to displace. The real cost is a weekly slot spent on the most levered name in a de-rating sector, when the credit market is explicitly pricing distress - unacceptable under the rulebook's risk gate regardless of the backlog. R:R also fails: a 10% trailing stop from $42.54 sits near $38.29, so 2:1 requires ~$51, well above the $44.91 prior close and demanding a ~20% rally against an active credit de-rating. Of today's list, CRWV and NBIS are the two whose declines are least likely to reverse, so even a relative-strength argument favours neither.

headlines: Amkor (AMKR) Q2 2026 earnings: record $1.9B revenue, CPO joins its tech platform, TSMC and NVIDIA long-term deals - Simple Tech Trend, 2026-10-07
83% of 2025 revenue from advanced packaging; largest US-headquartered OSAT, with US manufacturing expansion planned - Quartr investor presentation
Amkor Technology Reports Financial Results for the Third Quarter 2026 - quarterly revenue ~$1.99B, EPS guidance $0.65-$0.77
gappers.catalyst_detail: A date-bounded news search covering Nov 17-20 returned literally zero results for AMKR, so there is no company-specific catalyst behind this gap. Fundamentally the business is the strongest of the five: Amkor is the largest US-headquartered OSAT (outsourced semiconductor assembly and test), drew 83% of 2025 revenue from advanced packaging, posted a record $1.9B in Q2 2026 and ~$1.99B in Q3 2026, holds long-term agreements with TSMC and NVIDIA, and has added co-packaged optics (CPO) to its platform. Notably it traded BELOW its 20-day average volume on Nov 19 and still gapped -5.22% today.
gappers.why: Advanced packaging is the physical bottleneck for AI accelerators, so AMKR is indexed to the same AI capex narrative being sold - it falls by association through semis ETF and basket flows rather than on any judgement about its own order book. The below-average volume is the tell: this is mechanical, passive selling with no informed seller stepping up.
gappers.impact: This is the one name on the list that reads as a one-day headline/beta spike likely to mean-revert rather than a durable de-rating. A -5.22% gap on 0.4x average volume with no news is the signature of a sympathy move, and AMKR's advanced-packaging backlog is driven by foundry and accelerator demand that today's rotation does not touch. Sector read-through runs the other way for AMKR: it is being dragged by the neoclouds (NBIS, CRWV) and AI-power (BE) despite having a different, contract-backed revenue base.
gappers.horizon_reasoning: No company catalyst at all and below-average volume - a sympathy dislocation that should close when the complex stabilises, so it is a days-timeframe observation rather than a multi-week thesis.
gappers.opportunity_cost: No holding to displace. Against today's own list AMKR is the best-quality business and the only one whose decline looks genuinely unjustified, so it displaces the other four on merit - but it still fails the entry gate, because buying a -5.2% gap-down in an actively selling sector is counter-trend and violates 'follow sector momentum'. R:R is the hard block: a 10% trailing stop from $32.35 sits near $29.12, so 2:1 requires ~$38.80 (+20%), far above the $34.13 prior close - a mean-reversion bounce simply cannot pay 2:1 under a 10% stop. This is the structural 10%-stop/2:1-R:R conflict already flagged in the log, and AMKR is the cleanest illustration of it: the right read and still no admissible trade. Worth re-checking on a confirmed reversal with volume.
